subject: maths
title: Primary 6 Fraction Word Problems
seo_title: P6 Fraction Word Problems Worksheets: Free Primary 6 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus, PSLE Practice)
standard_text: Solving word problems involving the four operations on fractions
meta_desc: Free P6 fraction word problems for the PSLE: fraction of a remainder, finding the whole, before-and-after and the model method. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Always ask “a fraction of what?” Find the remainder first, then take the fraction of the remainder.
key_sub: Spent 1/3 of $60, then 1/4 of the rest: the rest is $40, so 1/4 of $40 = $10 (not 1/4 of $60).
body_html:
The big idea

Every fraction is a fraction of something. Before you calculate, ask: “a fraction of what?” Draw a bar model and work with units: find 1 unit first, then the number of units you need.

Fraction of a quantity

Divide by the denominator to find 1 unit. Multiply by the numerator.

Fraction of a remainder

When a question says “of the remainder” or “of the rest”, find the remainder first. Then take the fraction of the remainder, not of the whole.

Example

Siti had $60. She spent 13 of it on a book and 14 of the remainder on lunch. How much did she have left?

Book: 13 of $60 = $20. Remainder: $60 − $20 = $40. Lunch: 14 of $40 = $10. Left: $40 − $10 = $30.

Answer: $30

Finding the whole from a part

If you know the value of some units, find 1 unit, then multiply by the total number of units.

Example

Hui Min spent 35 of her money and had $24 left. How much did she have at first?

She has 5 − 3 = 2 units left. 2 units = $24, so 1 unit = $12. At first: 5 units = 5 × $12.

Answer: $60

Before-and-after problems

Look for the quantity that does not change (the total, the difference or one person’s amount) and use the same units for it before and after.

Example

Jun Jie had 35 as many stickers as Zhi Hao. After Zhi Hao gave Jun Jie 12 stickers, they had the same number. How many stickers did they have altogether?

Jun Jie: 3 units. Zhi Hao: 5 units. To be equal, both need 4 units, so Zhi Hao gave 1 unit. 1 unit = 12, and 8 units = 96.

Answer: 96 stickers

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Taking 14 of the whole ($60) when the question says 14 of the remainderFind the remainder first ($40), then 14 of $40 = $10
Adding fractions of different wholes: 13 + 14 = 712 spentChange the second fraction into a fraction of the whole: 14 × 23 = 16, so 13 + 16 = 12 spent
Finding one unit only and stopping (2 units = 12, so the answer is 6)Read the question again: multiply 1 unit by the number of units asked for
Using the part used when the question gives the part leftIf 35 is spent and $24 is left, then $24 is 2 units, not 3 units

faq.q: What fraction word problems come out in the PSLE?
faq.a: The PSLE often has fraction of a remainder, finding the whole from a part, comparing two people and before-and-after problems. Many of them are multi-step questions in Paper 2, so students should show their working.

faq.q: How do I teach fraction word problems with the model method?
faq.a: Draw a bar for the whole and cut it into equal units using the denominator. Label what you know and put “?” for the unknown, then find 1 unit first.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake in fraction of a remainder questions?
faq.a: Taking the fraction of the whole instead of the remainder. If Siti spent 1/3 of $60 and then 1/4 of the remainder, the second part is 1/4 of $40, not 1/4 of $60.

faq.q: Are fraction word problems in the MOE Primary 6 syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. The MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics Syllabus includes solving word problems involving the four operations on fractions, and Primary 6 students use them in multi-step problems.

items.q: The model shows $40 split into 5 equal units. Find 35 of $40.
The model shows 36 kg split into 4 equal units. Find 34 of 36 kg.
items.e: 4 units = 36 kg. 1 unit = 36 kg ÷ 4 = 9 kg. 3 units = 3 × 9 kg = 27 kg.

items.q: The model shows 27 ℓ split into 3 equal units. Find 23 of 27 ℓ.
items.e: 3 units = 27 ℓ. 1 unit = 27 ℓ ÷ 3 = 9 ℓ. 2 units = 2 × 9 ℓ = 18 ℓ.

items.q: The model shows 56 m split into 8 equal units. Find 58 of 56 m.
items.e: 8 units = 56 m. 1 unit = 56 m ÷ 8 = 7 m. 5 units = 5 × 7 m = 35 m.

items.q: The model shows $63 split into 7 equal units. Find 47 of $63.
Find 56 of $72.
Find 38 of 96 kg.
items.e: 8 units = 96 kg. 1 unit = 96 kg ÷ 8 = 12 kg. 3 units = 3 × 12 kg = 36 kg.

items.q: Find 49 of 54 m.
items.e: 9 units = 54 m. 1 unit = 54 m ÷ 9 = 6 m. 4 units = 4 × 6 m = 24 m.

items.q: Find 710 of 250 g.
Find 27 of 84 cm.
items.e: 7 units = 84 cm. 1 unit = 84 cm ÷ 7 = 12 cm. 2 units = 2 × 12 cm = 24 cm.

items.q: Find the value of 512 × 96.
items.e: 512 × 96 means 512 of 96. 12 units = 96. 1 unit = 96 ÷ 12 = 8. 5 units = 5 × 8 = 40.

items.q: Find the value of 35 × 85.
items.e: 35 × 85 means 35 of 85. 5 units = 85. 1 unit = 85 ÷ 5 = 17. 3 units = 3 × 17 = 51.

items.q: Find 34 of $6.
Find 25 of 1 h. Give your answer in minutes.
items.e: 1 h = 60 min. 1 unit = 60 min ÷ 5 = 12 min. 2 units = 2 × 12 min = 24 min. (1 h is 60 min, not 100 min.)

items.q: Find 38 of 1 kg. Give your answer in grams.
Find 56 of 3 ℓ. Give your answer in millilitres.
Find 35 of 2 m 50 cm. Give your answer in centimetres.
items.e: 2 m 50 cm = 250 cm. 1 unit = 250 cm ÷ 5 = 50 cm. 3 units = 3 × 50 cm = 150 cm. (Do not leave out the 50 cm.)

items.q: There are 48 students in the school hall. 58 of them are girls. How many boys are there?
items.e: The girls are 5 units out of 8, so the boys are 3 units. 1 unit = 48 ÷ 8 = 6. Boys: 3 × 6 = 18. (30 is the number of girls.)

items.q: A tank can hold 60 ℓ of water. It is 34 full. How much more water is needed to fill it?
items.e: The tank is 3 units full out of 4, so 1 unit is still empty. 1 unit = 60 ℓ ÷ 4 = 15 ℓ. (45 ℓ is the water already in the tank.)

items.q: Mrs Lim baked 72 pineapple tarts for Chinese New Year. She gave away 79 of them. How many tarts did she have left?
items.e: She gave away 7 units out of 9, so 2 units are left. 1 unit = 72 ÷ 9 = 8. Left: 2 × 8 = 16 tarts.

items.q: Siti had $60. She spent 13 of her money on a book and 14 of the remainder on lunch. How much did she spend on lunch?
items.e: Book: 13 of $60 = $20. Remainder: $60 − $20 = $40. Lunch: 14 of $40 = $10. (Take 14 of the remainder, not of $60.)

items.q: Mr Tan had 120 mandarin oranges. He gave 14 of them to his neighbours and 23 of the remainder to his relatives. How many mandarin oranges did he have left?
items.e: Neighbours: 14 of 120 = 30. Remainder: 120 − 30 = 90. Relatives: 23 of 90 = 60. Left: 90 − 60 = 30.

items.q: Mdm Wong had a roll of ribbon 72 m long. She used 58 of it to wrap gift boxes and 13 of the remainder to make bows. How many metres of ribbon did she use to make bows?
items.e: Gift boxes: 58 of 72 m = 45 m. Remainder: 72 m − 45 m = 27 m. Bows: 13 of 27 m = 9 m. (Take 13 of the remainder, not of 72 m.)

items.q: Wei Ming had 84 stickers. He gave 27 of them to his sister and 35 of the remainder to his friends. How many stickers did he give to his friends?
items.e: Sister: 27 of 84 = 24. Remainder: 84 − 24 = 60. Friends: 35 of 60 = 36. (Take 35 of the remainder, not of 84.)

items.q: A tank had 96 ℓ of water. 38 of the water was used to wash a car and 25 of the remainder was used to water the plants. How much water was left in the tank?
items.e: Car: 38 of 96 ℓ = 36 ℓ. Remainder: 96 ℓ − 36 ℓ = 60 ℓ. Plants: 25 of 60 ℓ = 24 ℓ. Left: 60 ℓ − 24 ℓ = 36 ℓ.

items.q: Priya had $90. She spent 25 of it on a pair of shoes and 13 of the remainder on a bag. How much did she spend altogether?
items.e: Shoes: 25 of $90 = $36. Remainder: $90 − $36 = $54. Bag: 13 of $54 = $18. Altogether: $36 + $18 = $54.

items.q: There were 450 people at a National Day concert. 25 of them were adults and 13 of the remainder were boys. The rest were girls. How many girls were there?
items.e: Adults: 25 of 450 = 180. Remainder: 450 − 180 = 270. Boys: 13 of 270 = 90. Girls: 270 − 90 = 180.

items.q: Mrs Ng baked 144 curry puffs. She sold 512 of them in the morning and 37 of the remainder in the afternoon. How many curry puffs did she sell in the afternoon?
items.e: Morning: 512 of 144 = 60. Remainder: 144 − 60 = 84. Afternoon: 37 of 84 = 36. (Take 37 of the remainder, not of 144.)

items.q: Jun Jie had $150 in his savings. He used 15 of it to buy a birthday present for his mother and 38 of the remainder to buy books. How much money did he have left?
items.e: Present: 15 of $150 = $30. Remainder: $150 − $30 = $120. Books: 38 of $120 = $45. Left: $120 − $45 = $75.

items.q: A drinks stall sold 240 drinks on Saturday. 38 of them were bubble tea and 15 of the remainder were kopi. How many cups of kopi were sold?
items.e: Bubble tea: 38 of 240 = 90. Remainder: 240 − 90 = 150. Kopi: 15 of 150 = 30. (Take 15 of the remainder, not of 240.)

items.q: Hafiz had $45. He spent 13 of it on a T-shirt and 14 of the remainder on lunch at a hawker centre. How much did he spend on lunch?
items.e: T-shirt: 13 of $45 = $15. Remainder: $45 − $15 = $30. Lunch: 14 of $30 = $7.50. (Take 14 of the remainder, not of $45.)

items.q: Chloe had 150 beads. She used 35 of them to make a necklace and 23 of the remainder to make a bracelet. How many beads did she use altogether?
items.e: Necklace: 35 of 150 = 90. Remainder: 150 − 90 = 60. Bracelet: 23 of 60 = 40. Altogether: 90 + 40 = 130.

items.q: Ethan had $80. He topped up his EZ-Link card with 14 of it and spent 35 of the remainder on books. How much money did he have left?
items.e: EZ-Link card: 14 of $80 = $20. Remainder: $80 − $20 = $60. Books: 35 of $60 = $36. Left: $60 − $36 = $24.

items.q: Xin Yi had 3 h of free time on Saturday. She spent 14 of the time reading and 23 of the remaining time at the swimming pool. How much free time did she have left? Give your answer in minutes.
items.e: 3 h = 180 min. Reading: 14 of 180 min = 45 min. Remainder: 180 − 45 = 135 min. Swimming: 23 of 135 min = 90 min. Left: 135 − 90 = 45 min.

items.q: Devi had 1 ℓ 500 ml of orange juice. She poured 15 of it into a glass and 25 of the remainder into a bottle. How much juice was left? Give your answer in millilitres.
items.e: 1 ℓ 500 ml = 1500 ml. Glass: 15 of 1500 ml = 300 ml. Remainder: 1500 − 300 = 1200 ml. Bottle: 25 of 1200 ml = 480 ml. Left: 1200 − 480 = 720 ml.

items.q: Nurul spent 14 of her money on a dress and 13 of the remainder on a bag. What fraction of her money did she spend on the bag?
items.e: Remainder: 1 − 14 = 34. Bag: 13 of 34 = 13 × 34 = 14.

items.q: Arjun spent 25 of his money on a game and 12 of the remainder on a book. What fraction of his money did he have left?
items.e: Remainder: 1 − 25 = 35. Book: 12 of 35 = 12 × 35 = 310. Left: 35 − 310 = 310.

items.q: Sarah used 13 of a packet of flour to make bread and 34 of the remainder to make a cake. What fraction of the packet of flour did she use for the cake?
items.e: Remainder: 1 − 13 = 23. Cake: 34 of 23 = 34 × 23 = 12.

items.q: A water tank was full. 35 of the water was used on Monday and 14 of the remainder was used on Tuesday. What fraction of the water was left?
items.e: Remainder: 1 − 35 = 25. Tuesday: 14 of 25 = 14 × 25 = 110. Left: 25 − 110 = 310.

items.q: Ryan spent 16 of his money at a hawker centre and 35 of the remainder at a bookshop. What fraction of his money did he spend altogether?
items.e: Remainder: 1 − 16 = 56. Bookshop: 35 of 56 = 35 × 56 = 12. Altogether: 16 + 12 = 23.

items.q: Mr Rahman had 48 m of rope. He used 38 of it to tie up a tent and 14 of it to make a fence for a garden bed. How much more rope did he use for the tent than for the fence?
items.e: 38 of 48 m = 18 m. 14 of 48 m = 12 m. Difference: 18 m − 12 m = 6 m. (You can also subtract first: 38 − 14 = 18, and 18 of 48 m = 6 m.)

items.q: There are 40 students in a P6 class. 35 of them take the bus to school and 14 of them walk. How many more students take the bus than walk?
items.e: 35 of 40 students = 24 students. 14 of 40 students = 10 students. Difference: 24 students − 10 students = 14 students. (You can also subtract first: 35 − 14 = 720, and 720 of 40 students = 14 students.)

items.q: Mrs Ng had $120. She spent 512 of it on groceries and 14 of it on a gift. How much more did she spend on groceries than on the gift?
items.e: 512 of $120 = $50. 14 of $120 = $30. Difference: $50 − $30 = $20. (You can also subtract first: 512 − 14 = 16, and 16 of $120 = $20.)

items.q: A hawker stall sold 360 plates of food in a day. 49 of them were chicken rice and 16 of them were laksa. How many more plates of chicken rice than laksa were sold?
items.e: 49 of 360 plates = 160 plates. 16 of 360 plates = 60 plates. Difference: 160 plates − 60 plates = 100 plates. (You can also subtract first: 49 − 16 = 518, and 518 of 360 plates = 100 plates.)

items.q: Sarah had $30 of pocket money. She saved 25 of it and spent 14 of it on snacks. How much more did she save than spend on snacks?
items.e: 25 of $30 = $12. 14 of $30 = $7.50. Difference: $12 − $7.50 = $4.50. (You can also subtract first: 25 − 14 = 320, and 320 of $30 = $4.50.)

items.q: A school garden has an area of 90 m². 25 of it is grass and 13 of it is flower beds. How much greater is the area of grass than the area of flower beds?
items.e: 25 of 90 m² = 36 m². 13 of 90 m² = 30 m². Difference: 36 m² − 30 m² = 6 m². (You can also subtract first: 25 − 13 = 115, and 115 of 90 m² = 6 m².)

items.q: Mei Ling ate 38 of a cake and her brother ate 16 of the same cake. How much more of the cake did Mei Ling eat than her brother?
items.e: Use a common denominator: 38 = 924 and 16 = 424. 924 − 424 = 524. (Rename both fractions before you subtract.)

items.q: Ali’s savings are 25 of Mei Ling’s savings. Mei Ling has $45 more than Ali. How much money does Ali have?
items.e: Ali has 2 units and Mei Ling has 5 units. The difference is 5 − 2 = 3 units. 3 units = $45, 1 unit = $15. Ali: 2 × $15 = $30. (Do not stop at 1 unit.)

items.q: Wei Ming has 34 as many stamps as Jun Jie. Jun Jie has 18 more stamps than Wei Ming. How many stamps do they have altogether?
items.e: Wei Ming has 3 units and Jun Jie has 4 units. The difference is 1 unit = 18. Altogether: 3 + 4 = 7 units = 7 × 18 = 126 stamps.

items.q: The mass of Box A is 58 of the mass of Box B. The total mass of the two boxes is 39 kg. What is the mass of Box A?
items.e: Box A has 5 units and Box B has 8 units: 13 units altogether. 13 units = 39 kg, 1 unit = 3 kg. Box A: 5 × 3 kg = 15 kg.

items.q: The volume of water in Tank A is 47 of the volume of water in Tank B. Tank B has 27 ℓ more water than Tank A. How much water is in Tank B?
items.e: Tank A has 4 units and Tank B has 7 units. The difference is 3 units = 27 ℓ, so 1 unit = 9 ℓ. Tank B: 7 × 9 ℓ = 63 ℓ.

items.q: Farah saved 23 as much as her brother Hafiz. Together they saved $90. How much more did Hafiz save than Farah?
items.e: Farah has 2 units and Hafiz has 3 units: 5 units altogether. 5 units = $90, 1 unit = $18. Hafiz saved 1 unit more: $18.

items.q: A ribbon was cut into two pieces. The shorter piece is 35 as long as the longer piece. The difference in their lengths is 24 cm. How long was the ribbon before it was cut?
items.e: Shorter piece: 3 units. Longer piece: 5 units. The difference is 2 units = 24 cm, so 1 unit = 12 cm. The ribbon: 8 units = 8 × 12 cm = 96 cm.

items.q: There are 34 as many boys as girls in a school choir. There are 63 pupils in the choir. How many girls are there?
items.e: Boys: 3 units. Girls: 4 units. 7 units = 63, 1 unit = 9. Girls: 4 × 9 = 36. (63 is all the pupils, not the boys.)

items.q: Ali had $72. He spent 13 of it on a game and 14 of the remainder on a book. How much more did he spend on the game than on the book?
items.e: Game: 13 of $72 = $24. Remainder: $72 − $24 = $48. Book: 14 of $48 = $12. Difference: $24 − $12 = $12. (14 of $72 = $18 is wrong: the book is 14 of the remainder.)

items.q: Devi had 120 beads. She used 38 of them for a bracelet and 25 of the remainder for a key chain. How many more beads did she use for the bracelet than for the key chain?
items.e: Bracelet: 38 of 120 = 45. Remainder: 120 − 45 = 75. Key chain: 25 of 75 = 30. Difference: 45 − 30 = 15 beads.

items.q: Mrs Lim had 2 kg of flour. She used 14 of it to make bread and 45 of the remainder to make a cake. How much more flour did she use for the cake than for the bread? Give your answer in grams.
items.e: 2 kg = 2000 g. Bread: 14 of 2000 g = 500 g. Remainder: 1500 g. Cake: 45 of 1500 g = 1200 g. Difference: 1200 − 500 = 700 g.

items.q: Jun Jie spent 16 of his money on food and 12 of the remainder on a book. How much more did he spend on the book than on food? Give your answer as a fraction of his money.
items.e: Book: 12 of 56 = 512. Food: 16 = 212. Difference: 512 − 212 = 312 = 14. (12 − 16 = 13 is wrong: the two fractions are of different wholes.)

items.q: Kavya ate 14 of a pizza. Then Ryan ate 13 of what was left. Who ate more pizza?
items.e: 34 was left after Kavya ate. Ryan ate 13 of 34 = 14. Both ate 14 of the pizza, so they ate the same amount.

items.q: Ahmad cycled a 36 km route. He cycled 13 of it before lunch and 34 of the remaining distance after lunch. How much farther did he cycle after lunch than before lunch?
items.e: Before lunch: 13 of 36 km = 12 km. Remaining: 24 km. After lunch: 34 of 24 km = 18 km. Difference: 18 − 12 = 6 km.

sets.title: Finding the whole from a part

items.q: 27 of the students in a P6 class wear spectacles. 12 students wear spectacles. How many students are there in the class?
items.e: 2 units = 12 students. 1 unit = 12 students ÷ 2 = 6 students. The whole is 7 units: 7 × 6 students = 42 students.

items.q: 35 of a sum of money is $36. What is the whole sum of money?
items.e: 3 units = $36. 1 unit = $36 ÷ 3 = $12. The whole is 5 units: 5 × $12 = $60.

items.q: Mr Kumar has read 58 of a book. He has read 150 pages. How many pages are there in the book?
items.e: 5 units = 150 pages. 1 unit = 150 pages ÷ 5 = 30 pages. The whole is 8 units: 8 × 30 pages = 240 pages.

items.q: A tank is 38 full. It has 24 ℓ of water in it. What is the capacity of the tank?
items.e: 3 units = 24 ℓ. 1 unit = 24 ℓ ÷ 3 = 8 ℓ. The whole is 8 units: 8 × 8 ℓ = 64 ℓ.

items.q: 49 of the pupils in the canteen bought chicken rice. 36 pupils bought chicken rice. How many pupils were in the canteen?
items.e: 4 units = 36 pupils. 1 unit = 36 pupils ÷ 4 = 9 pupils. The whole is 9 units: 9 × 9 pupils = 81 pupils.

items.q: Siti saved 710 of her pocket money. She saved $42. How much pocket money did she have?
items.e: 7 units = $42. 1 unit = $42 ÷ 7 = $6. The whole is 10 units: 10 × $6 = $60.

items.q: Hui Min spent 35 of her money and had $24 left. How much money did she have at first?
items.e: 35 was used, so 5 − 3 = 2 units are left. 2 units = $24, 1 unit = $12. At first: 5 units = 5 × $12 = $60. ($24 is the part left, not the part used.)

items.q: Arjun gave away 59 of his marbles and had 28 marbles left. How many marbles did he have at first?
items.e: 59 was used, so 9 − 5 = 4 units are left. 4 units = 28 marbles, 1 unit = 7 marbles. At first: 9 units = 9 × 7 marbles = 63 marbles. (28 marbles is the part left, not the part used.)

items.q: After 38 of the water in a tank was used, 45 ℓ of water was left. How much water was in the tank at first?
items.e: 38 was used, so 8 − 3 = 5 units are left. 5 units = 45 ℓ, 1 unit = 9 ℓ. At first: 8 units = 8 × 9 ℓ = 72 ℓ. (45 ℓ is the part left, not the part used.)

items.q: A fruit seller sold 712 of his durians and had 40 durians left. How many durians did he have at first?
items.e: 712 was used, so 12 − 7 = 5 units are left. 5 units = 40 durians, 1 unit = 8 durians. At first: 12 units = 12 × 8 durians = 96 durians. (40 durians is the part left, not the part used.)

items.q: Ryan used 23 of the value on his EZ-Link card and $5.40 was left. How much was on the card at first?
items.e: 23 was used, so 3 − 2 = 1 unit is left. 1 unit = $5.40. At first: 3 units = 3 × $5.40 = $16.20. ($5.40 is the part left, not the part used.)

items.q: In the model, 3 of the 8 equal units have a value of 27. What is the value of the whole bar?
items.e: 3 units = 27. 1 unit = 27 ÷ 3 = 9. The whole bar is 8 units: 8 × 9 = 72.

items.q: In the model, 3 of the 5 equal units have a value of 51. What is the value of the whole bar?
items.e: 3 units = 51. 1 unit = 51 ÷ 3 = 17. The whole bar is 5 units: 5 × 17 = 85.

items.q: In the model, the 4 white units have a value of 32. What is the value of the whole bar?
items.e: 4 units = 32. 1 unit = 32 ÷ 4 = 8. The whole bar is 7 units: 7 × 8 = 56.

items.q: In the model, the 7 white units have a value of 49. What is the value of the whole bar?
items.e: 7 units = 49. 1 unit = 49 ÷ 7 = 7. The whole bar is 9 units: 9 × 7 = 63.

items.q: Siti spent 13 of her money on a book and 14 of the remainder on lunch. She spent $10 on lunch. How much money did she have at first?
items.e: Lunch = 14 of the remainder, so the remainder = 4 × $10 = $40. The remainder is 23 of her money: 2 units = $40, 1 unit = $20. At first: 3 × $20 = $60.

items.q: Mr Tan gave 14 of his mandarin oranges to his neighbours and 23 of the remainder to his relatives. He had 30 mandarin oranges left. How many did he have at first?
items.e: He had 13 of the remainder left, so the remainder = 3 × 30 = 90. The remainder is 34 of all: 3 units = 90, 1 unit = 30. At first: 4 × 30 = 120. (1 − 14 − 23 = 112 is wrong: the fractions are of different wholes.)

items.q: Nurul spent 25 of her money on a bag and 12 of the remainder on shoes. She had $45 left. How much money did she have at first?
items.e: She had 12 of the remainder left, so the remainder = 2 × $45 = $90. The remainder is 35 of her money: 3 units = $90, 1 unit = $30. At first: 5 × $30 = $150.

items.q: A tank was full of water. 14 of the water was used in the morning and 13 of the remaining water was used in the afternoon. 36 ℓ of water was left. How much water was in the tank at first?
items.e: 23 of the remaining water was left, so the remaining water = 36 ℓ ÷ 2 × 3 = 54 ℓ. It is 34 of the full tank: 3 units = 54 ℓ, 1 unit = 18 ℓ. At first: 4 × 18 ℓ = 72 ℓ.

items.q: Ethan spent 38 of his savings on a watch and 25 of the remainder on a bag. He spent $60 on the bag. How much were his savings at first?
items.e: The bag = 25 of the remainder, so the remainder = $60 ÷ 2 × 5 = $150. The remainder is 58 of his savings: 5 units = $150, 1 unit = $30. At first: 8 × $30 = $240.

items.q: 23 of Wei Ming’s marbles is equal to 34 of Hafiz’s marbles. They have 85 marbles altogether. How many marbles does Wei Ming have?
items.e: Make the numerators the same: 23 = 69 and 34 = 68. So Wei Ming has 9 units and Hafiz has 8 units. 17 units = 85, 1 unit = 5. Wei Ming: 9 × 5 = 45 marbles.

items.q: In a school hall, 35 of the boys is equal to 12 of the girls. There are 26 more girls than boys. How many girls are there?
items.e: Make the numerators the same: 35 = 35 and 12 = 36. Boys: 5 units. Girls: 6 units. The difference is 1 unit = 26. Girls: 6 × 26 = 156.

items.q: 34 of the mass of Box A is equal to 25 of the mass of Box B. Box B is 21 kg heavier than Box A. What is the total mass of the two boxes?
items.e: Make the numerators the same: 34 = 68 and 25 = 615. Box A: 8 units. Box B: 15 units. The difference is 7 units = 21 kg, so 1 unit = 3 kg. Total: 23 units = 23 × 3 kg = 69 kg. (Do not use the denominators 4 and 5 as the units.)

items.q: Jun Jie had 35 as many stickers as Zhi Hao. After Zhi Hao gave Jun Jie 12 stickers, they had the same number of stickers. How many stickers did they have altogether?
items.e: Jun Jie: 3 units. Zhi Hao: 5 units. To have the same number, each needs 4 units, so Zhi Hao gave 1 unit. 1 unit = 12. Altogether: 8 units = 8 × 12 = 96 stickers.

items.q: Priya had 47 as much money as her sister Devi. After Devi gave Priya $30, they had the same amount of money. How much money did Priya have at first?
items.e: Priya: 4 units. Devi: 7 units. The difference is 3 units. After Devi gives $30, the difference is 0, so 3 units = 2 × $30 = $60. 1 unit = $20. Priya at first: 4 × $20 = $80.

items.q: Raju had 38 as many cards as Arjun. After Raju bought 20 more cards, he had 78 as many cards as Arjun. How many cards does Arjun have?
items.e: Arjun’s cards do not change: 8 units. Raju went from 3 units to 7 units, so 4 units = 20 and 1 unit = 5. Arjun: 8 × 5 = 40 cards.

items.q: A tank was 25 full of water. After 18 ℓ of water was poured in, it was 45 full. What is the capacity of the tank?
items.e: The water went up from 25 to 45, which is 25 of the tank. 2 units = 18 ℓ, 1 unit = 9 ℓ. Capacity: 5 units = 45 ℓ.

items.q: A box had some red beads and blue beads. 38 of the beads were red. After Siti put in 12 more red beads, 12 of the beads were red. How many beads were in the box at first?
items.e: At first: red 3 units, blue 5 units. The blue beads do not change. After: red = blue = 5 units. The red beads went up by 2 units = 12, so 1 unit = 6. At first: 8 units = 48 beads.

items.q: Mr Kumar spent 14 of his money on a watch and 23 of the remainder on a pair of shoes. The shoes cost $36 more than the watch. How much money did he have at first?
items.e: Watch: 1 unit out of 4. The remainder is 3 units; the shoes are 23 of it = 2 units. The shoes cost 1 unit more than the watch: 1 unit = $36. At first: 4 × $36 = $144.

items.q: Mr Rahman spent 58 of his money on a bicycle and 13 of the remainder on a helmet. The bicycle cost $180 more than the helmet. How much did the helmet cost?
items.e: Bicycle: 5 units out of 8. Remainder: 3 units; helmet: 13 of 3 units = 1 unit. The difference is 5 − 1 = 4 units = $180, so 1 unit = $45. The helmet cost $45.

items.q: Kavya read 14 of a storybook on Monday and 23 of the remaining pages on Tuesday. She read 30 more pages on Tuesday than on Monday. How many pages did she read on Tuesday?
items.e: Monday: 1 unit out of 4. Remainder: 3 units; Tuesday: 23 of 3 units = 2 units. The difference is 1 unit = 30 pages. Tuesday: 2 × 30 = 60 pages.

items.q: 35 of the pupils in a school are girls. 14 of the girls and 12 of the boys wear spectacles. 70 pupils wear spectacles. How many girls are there in the school?
items.e: Girls with spectacles: 14 × 35 = 320. Boys with spectacles: 12 × 25 = 15 = 420. Together: 720 of the pupils = 70, so 120 = 10 and all the pupils = 200. Girls: 35 of 200 = 120.

items.q: Xin Yi gave 13 of her stickers to her brother and 14 of the remainder to her sister. She had 36 stickers left. How many stickers did she give to her sister?
items.e: 36 stickers are 34 of the remainder, so the remainder = 36 ÷ 3 × 4 = 48. Sister: 14 of 48 = 12.

items.q: Chloe spent 25 of her money on pens and 34 of the remainder on files. She had $4.50 left. How much did she spend on pens?
items.e: $4.50 is 14 of the remainder, so the remainder = 4 × $4.50 = $18. The remainder is 35 of her money: 3 units = $18, 1 unit = $6. Pens: 2 units = $12.

items.q: At a CCA fair, 25 of the students signed up for sports and 13 of the rest signed up for uniformed groups. The other 120 students signed up for clubs. How many students signed up for uniformed groups?
items.e: The 120 students are 23 of the rest, so the rest = 120 ÷ 2 × 3 = 180. Uniformed groups: 13 of 180 = 60.

items.q: Mr Tan drove from his home to Changi Airport. He stopped for breakfast after driving 25 of the distance. After breakfast, he drove 12 of the remaining distance and then had 12 km left to drive. How far was his home from the airport?
items.e: 12 km is 12 of the remaining distance, so the remaining distance = 24 km. It is 35 of the whole: 3 units = 24 km, 1 unit = 8 km. Whole: 5 units = 40 km.

items.q: Mrs Lim poured 27 of a bottle of milk into a jug and 12 of the rest into cups. 1 ℓ 250 ml of milk was left in the bottle. How much milk was in the bottle at first?
items.e: 1 ℓ 250 ml = 1250 ml. It is 12 of the rest, so the rest = 2 × 1250 ml = 2500 ml. The rest is 57 of the milk: 5 units = 2500 ml, 1 unit = 500 ml. At first: 7 × 500 ml = 3500 ml = 3 ℓ 500 ml.

items.q: Hafiz and Ryan had the same amount of money. Hafiz spent 14 of his money and Ryan spent $42. Then Hafiz had 3 times as much money as Ryan. How much money did each boy have at first?
items.e: Each boy had 4 units. Hafiz has 3 units left, so Ryan has 1 unit left (3 times as much). Ryan spent 3 units = $42, so 1 unit = $14. At first: 4 × $14 = $56 each.

items.q: In a club, the number of boys was 35 of the number of girls. Then 6 more boys joined and 4 girls left. After that, there were as many boys as girls. How many members were in the club at first?
items.e: Boys: 3 units. Girls: 5 units. After: 3 units + 6 = 5 units − 4, so 2 units = 6 + 4 = 10 and 1 unit = 5. At first: 8 units = 40 members.

items.q: Sarah gave 12 of her sweets and 3 more to Ethan. Then she gave 12 of the remaining sweets and 3 more to Chloe. She had 6 sweets left. How many sweets did she have at first?
items.e: Work backwards. Before the last 3: 6 + 3 = 9, which is half, so before Chloe: 18. Before the 3 for Ethan: 18 + 3 = 21, which is half, so at first: 42. She had 42 sweets.
